data.why: The app ships three curated real qPCR datasets (Boggy dilution series, Rutledge high-throughput screen, reps technical replicates) loadable in-app via the 'Load Example Data' dropdown or uploadable as CSVs, matching the app's expected wide-format Cycles+well-column schema.

goals: Estimate absolute initial template concentration (D0) for each well from a raw amplification curve without running a standard curve
Fit the MAK2 kinetic model to a dilution series and check that D0 estimates track the expected 10-fold dilution steps
Quantify uncertainty on D0 via bootstrap confidence intervals and judge whether a well's fit is trustworthy
Assess technical replicate precision (CV of D0) across replicate wells at a given concentration
Identify and flag problematic wells (no-template controls, very late or noisy amplification, failed fits) before reporting results
Export per-well fit parameters, quality metrics, and plots for a batch of wells

review.summary: The tree follows the MAK2 batch workflow accurately: load, group replicates and declare the dilution, fit, judge replicate and dilution quality, export. Its cited screens hold up, and its general and specific wording is mostly clean. It misses the interface's headline purpose of converting D0 to absolute copy numbers, and it wrongly says bootstrap CIs are absent when they sit behind the single-well fit mode, so it needs those added before filing.
